history.dynasty: Somavanshi dynasty (9th-11th centuries CE) claimed for the site's origins by one listing (verify); present structure dated to the 18th century A.D. by another listing (verify).
history.period: Ancient site; present temple dated 18th century A.D. by one source (verify) - dating conflicts across sources.
history.summary: The Nilamadhab (Nilamadhava) Temple at Kantilo, Khandapada block, Nayagarh district, Odisha, is a famous ancient Vishnu temple on the right bank of the Mahanadi river at the confluence of the Mahanadi, Kuanria and Kusumi rivers - called the Triveni Sangam of Odisha. It stands on twin hills (Brahmadri/Himadri) amid forest, with the river flowing on three sides giving it an island-like appearance. The temple occupies a central place in the Jagannath cult: legend says the Sabara (tribal) chief Biswabasu secretly worshipped the deity as 'Kitung' in a cave in the Brahmadri hills, the deity being first worshipped as an Indranila gem image named 'Nilamadhava'; the daru (wooden) murti came much later at Puri under King Indradyumna. The temple structure is a miniature of the Puri Jagannath temple - rekha vimana, pidha jagamohana, garuda mandapa - and its daily rituals mirror those of the Puri Shreemandir, including worship of Patitapabana. A perennial spring, Brahma Kunda, flows near the temple (per one listing, verify). Kantilo is known for brass and bell-metal crafts sold as souvenirs. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV says 'Nayagarh' (the district), but the temple is at Kantilo, about 33 km from Nayagarh town and about 78-82 km from Bhubaneswar. Do not confuse with the similarly-named shrine of Nilamadhava inside the Puri Jagannath complex.

name: Nilamadhab Temple
town: Kantilo (CSV town 'Nayagarh' corrected - the temple is at Kantilo in Khandapada block, ~33 km from Nayagarh town, Nayagarh district)
town_description: Kantilo is a temple town in the Khandapada block of Nayagarh district, Odisha, about 33 km from Nayagarh town and 78-82 km from Bhubaneswar, on the banks of the Mahanadi river. It is famous for the Nilamadhab Vishnu temple on twin hills at the Triveni Sangam (confluence of the Mahanadi, Kuanria and Kusumi), and for local brass and bell-metal craft. Nearby attractions include the Bhattarika temple and the Deojhar waterfall.

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar - the closest airport; Kantilo is about 78-82 km from Bhubaneswar (verify).
travel.railway: Nayagarh Town station is the nearest railway station (per one listing, verify); most visitors disembark at Bhubaneswar and take buses to Kantilo.
travel.road: Kantilo is well connected by road with regular bus services; about 33 km from Nayagarh town on the Nayagarh-Kantilo road (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Magha Saptami (January-February) and the Magha Ekadashi fair are the peak pilgrimage occasions. Prasad is served about 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM per one listing (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 5:00 AM-2:00 PM and 3:00-10:00 PM daily (verify - from a single listing whose other transport details were unreliable; confirm locally).
